events.text: Momofuku Ando puts the first instant noodles on sale in Japan
The first machine-sliced loaves go on sale from a bakery in Missouri
Coca-Cola goes on sale as a soda fountain drink in Atlanta
Peter Durand is granted a British patent for preserving food in sealed tins

reveal.explanation: Durand's patent for food sealed in tins was granted in 1810, three-quarters of a century before Coca-Cola was first poured in Atlanta in 1886. Sliced bread reached the shops in 1928, and instant noodles followed thirty years later in 1958.

sources.excerpt: The patent (No 3372) was granted on August 25, 1810 by George III.
The first sales were at Jacob's Pharmacy in Atlanta, Georgia, on May 8, 1886, where it initially sold for five cents a glass.
The first commercial use of the machine was by the Chillicothe Baking Company of Chillicothe, Missouri, who sold their first slices on July 7, 1928.
They were first marketed on 25 August 1958 by Ando's company, Nissin, under the brand name Chikin Ramen.

editorNotes: Tins: Nicolas Appert is named on the same page as the man who developed the preserving technique, but he used glass vessels and his French award falls in a different frame, so the patent for tins is credited to Peter Durand, granted on 25 August 1810 and unhedged as to date; the page adds that Durand's idea was communicated to him by the French inventor Philippe de Girard and that he sold the patent on in 1812, so the text names the patent rather than the invention. Coca-Cola: the drink was developed in 1886 and first sold at Jacob's Pharmacy in Atlanta on 8 May 1886; the rival dates on the page are the first bottling at Vicksburg in 1894 and the first bottling company at Chattanooga in 1899, both later and both about bottles rather than the fountain. Sliced bread: Rohwedder built a prototype in 1912 that burned, and had a working machine only in 1928; Battle Creek in Michigan has a competing claim to be the first city to sell bread cut by his machine, but the page says no documentation supports it and the year is 1928 either way, with the lede giving the same year for the first sale. Instant noodles: Chikin Ramen was first marketed on 25 August 1958, and Nissin's Cup Noodles of 1971 was set aside as the later product.
